replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

- Automated abuse reachable: yes — "The login page is internet-facing" and the reset request form takes an email. Brute force of token (#5), enumeration (#6), mail flooding (#7) are covered. Not covered: the design states the user "sets a new password" with no strength or breached-password requirement, enabling later guessing/credential stuffing against the internet-facing login — not covered.
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing other people's content: design has none ("a public page where the user sets a new password") — not applicable.
- Sensitive account change with no record of who did it: yes — "sets a new password and is logged in immediately" with no mention of notifying the account owner or recording the change — not covered (listed threats cover reuse/stolen link, not absence of notification/audit).
- Personal/account pages browsers or CDNs could store: the reset page is public and token-bearing; token leakage through history/logs/referrer is already covered by listed threat 4 — covered.
- Attacker text into logs, exports, emails, headers: design states only "request a reset link by email address" with no templating or export described — not applicable (build-dependent).
- Single-reviewer items: MFA bypass, Host-header link base and client-supplied account id all depend on facts the design does not state (no second factor, no link-base source, no posted identifier) — excluded.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-01",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["reset request form", "reset email", "token link", "reset page", "login page", "session issuance"],
    "dataStores": ["user accounts", "reset tokens"],
    "externalServices": ["email provider"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["internet to public reset page", "email delivery"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "credentials"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Password change leaves no trace: owner is not notified and the change is not recorded",
      "scenario": "An attacker who reaches the reset link (shared mailbox, synced device) sets a new password and is signed in. The design mentions no confirmation mail to the account owner and no record of when or from where the password was changed, so the victim gets no warning signal and support cannot tell a legitimate reset from a takeover. Abuse of resets across many accounts stays invisible, and a user whose account is misused can deny or cannot disprove the change.",
      "component": "Reset page / password change",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Clicking it opens a public page where the user sets a new password and is logged in immediately." },
        { "quote": "Users who forget their password request a reset link by email address." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nobody tells the real owner their password changed, and there is no log of the change, so a hijack goes unnoticed and cannot be investigated.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Notify and record every password reset",
        "given": "a reset token is redeemed and a new password is set",
        "when": "the change is committed",
        "then": "send a notification to the account's registered address and write an audit record (timestamp, source IP, user agent, token id) that support can review"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "No password strength or breach check when the new password is set",
      "scenario": "The reset page lets the user set any new password; the design states no minimum length, no rejection of known-breached or trivial values. Users pick weak passwords here, and an attacker then scripts guesses against the internet-facing login page to take over those accounts without needing the reset flow at all.",
      "component": "Reset page password field",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "medium", "reach": "many", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "opens a public page where the user sets a new password and is logged in immediately. The login page is internet-facing." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.1.7"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-521"],
      "plainLanguage": "The reset page accepts any password, so people can set easy ones that attackers guess on the public login page.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce password policy on reset",
        "given": "a user submits a new password on the reset page",
        "when": "the password is validated server-side",
        "then": "reject passwords shorter than the policy minimum or present in a breached-password list, and return a clear error without setting the password"
      }
    }
  ]
}
